# Build a Custom Morning Briefing with News, Weather, and Calendar in Alexa+

> **In short:** In the Alexa app you can build one Routine that reads your linked calendar, today's weather, and a short news briefing when you say "Alexa, good morning." You'll need an Alexa+ subscription, which Amazon describes as its next-generation, AI-powered Alexa.

By the end of this guide, you'll have a single voice command that kicks off your day with the three things you actually need to know: what's on your calendar, what the weather will do, and what's happening in the world. It's a small setup, but once it works, it quietly replaces ten minutes of phone-checking every morning — and it works for anyone in the room who just says "good morning" to your Echo.

## Before you start
- An **Alexa+ subscription** (Amazon describes this as the paid next-generation tier — check Amazon's official pricing page for the latest details before you start).
- The **Alexa app** on your phone, signed in to the same Amazon account your Echo device uses.
- An **Alexa-enabled speaker** (Echo, Echo Dot, or any device on your Alexa account) placed where you'll usually be in the morning.
- A **calendar account ready to link** — Google, Microsoft, or Apple/iCloud all work.
- About **10–15 minutes** for the first setup; tweaking later takes seconds.

## Step 1 — Open Routines in the Alexa app
Open the **Alexa app** on your phone — it's the one with the light blue ring icon, separate from the Amazon Shopping app. Sign in with the same Amazon account that your Echo device is registered to, if it doesn't happen automatically. From the home screen, look at the **bottom navigation bar**: you should see tabs labeled something like Home, Communicate, Play, and Devices. Tap **More** or look for a **menu icon** (three lines or three dots) in the top-right corner to reveal the full menu — **Routines** is usually listed there under "More" or "Things to Try".

💬 Example: you don't need to type anything here, but if the app asks you to confirm your account, just tap **Continue** to proceed.

You'll know it worked when the Routines screen appears, showing any routines you've already made (likely none) and a button to create a new one.

## Step 2 — Start a new routine and give it a name
Tap the **Create Routine** button (or a **+** icon, depending on your app version). A new screen appears asking for two things: a **name** for the routine, and a list of actions it will run. First, tap into the **name field** at the top and type something easy to recognize — "Morning Briefing" works perfectly. The name only shows up inside the app, so it doesn't have to match the phrase you'll say out loud. If your app doesn't show a "Create Routine" button right away, look for **Add**, **New Routine**, or a **+** floating button at the bottom of the list.

💬 Example: type **Morning Briefing** as the routine name.

You'll know it worked when the routine name appears at the top of the screen and you see empty sections labeled something like **"When this happens"** and **"Add action"**.

## Step 3 — Set the voice trigger
Find the section labeled **"When this happens"** (it might say "When" or "Trigger" depending on your version). Tap it, then choose **Voice** from the list of trigger types. A text field appears asking for the phrase Alexa should listen for. Type **good morning** — or pick one of the suggested short phrases your app offers. Try to keep the phrase short; the more words you add, the more chances Alexa will mishear you, especially first thing in the day. Skip optional settings like "device" unless you want to limit the trigger to one specific Echo.

💬 Example: type **good morning** as the trigger phrase.

You'll know it worked when the trigger shows up in the routine summary as "Voice: good morning" and the screen moves down to the action section.

## Step 4 — Add the calendar action
Scroll down to **Add action** (or just "Actions") and tap it. A menu appears with categories like Communication, Music, News, Weather, Calendar, and more. Choose **Calendar** — or, if your app shows it, the shortcut called **"Tell me about my day"**, which Amazon describes as a way to summarize your agenda in one sentence. If your calendar isn't already linked, the app will walk you through connecting your Google, Microsoft, or iCloud account. Pick the account you actually use, then tap **Allow** on the permission screens that follow. The action is now attached to your routine.

💬 Example: if prompted, choose **Google Calendar** (or whichever service holds your real events) and tap **Allow**.

You'll know it worked when the action shows up in the routine as a card labeled something like "Read calendar events" or "Tell me about my day."

## Step 5 — Add the weather action
Stay inside the Actions menu and tap **Add action** again to add a second one. Choose **Weather** from the category list. Some app versions ask you to pick a specific device to read the forecast on; choose the Echo you'll be closest to in the morning — usually the one in your bedroom or kitchen. The app will use your device's location by default, but you can change it to a different city if you commute or travel regularly. Once you confirm, the weather action appears as another card in your routine, sitting below the calendar one.

💬 Example: set the location to your **home city** so the forecast matches your real day.

You'll know it worked when two action cards now appear in the routine list: one for the calendar, one for the weather, stacked in that order.

## Step 6 — Add the news action
Tap **Add action** once more and pick **News**. You'll see a list of available news providers — choose one you already trust, or pick the default option if your app shows one (Amazon describes Flash Briefing as a short, mixable audio summary). The default usually pulls about two to five minutes of audio, which is a comfortable length for a morning routine. Add just one news provider at first; you can stack more later if it feels too short. After you confirm, the routine now has three actions lined up in order: calendar, weather, news.

💬 Example: select a single trusted news provider like **NPR** or your local station, and keep the briefing length on **short**.

You'll know it worked when three action cards are visible in the routine list, in the order calendar → weather → news.

## Step 7 — Save and test your routine
Tap **Save** in the top-right corner to lock in your routine — if you don't see Save, look for a **checkmark** or **Done** button instead. The app drops you back to the Routines list, where your new "Morning Briefing" routine appears with a toggle to enable or disable it; make sure the toggle is **on** (usually blue). Now test it: stand within earshot of your Echo and clearly say **"Alexa, good morning."** Alexa should respond by reading your calendar events first, then the weather forecast, then a short news briefing. If anything is missing or the order feels off, come back to the routine and drag the action cards into the order you want.

💬 Example: say **"Alexa, good morning"** clearly, then wait silently for the full briefing to play through.

You'll know it worked when Alexa speaks all three pieces in order — calendar, weather, news — without you needing to ask a follow-up question.

## Common mistakes
- **Forgetting to link the calendar first.** If you add the calendar action before your Google, Microsoft, or iCloud account is connected, Alexa will quietly skip your events. Fix: open **Settings → Calendars** in the Alexa app, link the account you actually use, then return to your routine.
- **Using a trigger phrase that's too long.** "Alexa, please give me my full morning briefing now" is hard to catch accurately, especially over background noise. Fix: keep the phrase to two or three short, common words like **"good morning"**.
- **Reordering the actions by accident.** If news ends up playing before the weather, your morning feels scrambled. Fix: in the routine editor, **press and hold** an action card and drag it into the order you want — calendar, then weather, then news.
- **The routine toggle is off.** A perfect routine won't run if the switch next to its name is off. Fix: on the main Routines screen, slide the toggle next to **Morning Briefing** to **on**.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** anyone in your home — partner, kids, roommates — can trigger the briefing just by saying "good morning" to the Echo. No buttons, no phone unlock, no apps to open.
- **For your business or work:** the calendar piece doubles as a quick stand-up prompt for anyone who runs remote meetings or has back-to-back calls; you'll hear what's coming before you even reach for your laptop.
- **If you're just getting started:** keep the routine to those three actions for the first week. Once it feels automatic, add one more — like a one-line traffic update for your commute — so the briefing grows with you instead of overwhelming you on day one.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app right now and create the routine — even if you stop after Step 3, you'll already have the trigger phrase working, and the rest is just three more taps per action.
